usage: xo <command> [arguments]

commands:
  build     compile to static binaries (the host, or --targets)
  run       build for the host and run
  test      run test blocks, property tests, and contract fuzzing
  check     parse and type check the modules under each directory
  parse     parse .xo files and report syntax diagnostics
  fmt       rewrite .xo files in the one canonical layout
  fix       apply the machine fixes of check diagnostics
  vet       advisory checks (never errors)
  query     semantic queries: type, def, callers, effects, holes, api, ...
  edit      semantic edits: rename, add-field, change-sig
  doc       Markdown documentation from doc comments
  explain   long form explanation of a diagnostic code
  init      write xo.mod for a new module
  get       require, upgrade, or remove a module
  mod       tidy, accept-effects, clean, proxy serve
  vendor    copy every selected module version into vendor/
  publish   check a release against the previous version tag
  audit     supply chain report of the dependencies
  bind      bind Go packages (use go) or C headers (use c)
  dump      print the task tree of a running Xo program
  replay    rerun a recorded trace or crash bundle offline
  trace     Perfetto JSON and a summary of a native execution trace
  lsp       Language Server Protocol server on stdin/stdout
  mcp       Model Context Protocol server on stdin/stdout
  serve     keep checked programs in memory for check and query
  version   print the toolchain version and the host target

Run "xo <command> -h" for a command's usage and flags.
A command that takes directories also takes DIR/... (xo check ./...).
Every command accepts --offline (XO_OFFLINE=1: never fetch; a missing
module is XO1303) and --workspace=off (XO_WORK=off: ignore xo.work).
